papers.title: A folate receptor-targeted NIR-II probe improves intraoperative imaging and surgery of metastatic ovarian cancer.
papers.summary: Develops a folate receptor-alpha-targeted NIR-II imaging probe with an albumin-binding 4-(4-iodophenyl)butanoic acid moiety, prolonging circulation and tumor accumulation. In murine peritoneal metastasis models it visualized occult lesions undetectable by eye, outperforming clinical probe OTL38 in sensitivity (90.2% vs 78.75%), including sub-3-mm lesions, enabling precision fluorescence-guided surgery.

papers.title: Targeting the ENO1 metabolic checkpoint via microenvironment-responsive nanotherapeutics promotes postinfarction cardiac repair.
papers.summary: Identifies enolase 1 (ENO1) as a metabolic checkpoint driving inflammatory macrophage dysfunction after myocardial infarction. An acid-responsive nanocarrier (PeCS) delivers siENO1 to infarct macrophages, suppressing glycolytic flux and lactate accumulation and relieving KLF4 inhibition, reducing infarct size, fibrosis, and cardiomyocyte apoptosis while improving ventricular function in mice.

papers.title: Macrophage-supported metabolic adaptation drives tumor survival under nutrient stress.
papers.summary: In nutrient-limited triple-negative breast cancer, hypoxia-reprogrammed macrophages secrete ornithine, which responsive tumor cells divert into proline biosynthesis, supporting oxidative pentose phosphate pathway activity during glutamine deprivation. Myeloid-cell depletion reduced tumor growth, revealing macrophage-tumor metabolic crosstalk underlying resistance to glutamine-targeted therapies.

papers.title: Tumor cell-intrinsic stress states drive sensitivity to CAR T cell therapy in pancreatic cancer.
papers.summary: Integrating in vivo CRISPR screens, single-cell genomics, and immunocompetent orthotopic pancreatic cancer models, the authors identify oxidative and proteotoxic stress pathways as CAR T response modulators. Disrupting KEAP1 or SLC33A1, or NRF2 pathway hyperactivation, sensitizes tumors to CAR T killing, suggesting genotype-based patient stratification.

papers.title: An immunocompetent, multifluorescent resource for real-time analysis of osteosarcoma progression, metastasis, and response to therapy.
papers.summary: Presents the RoCCIA mouse, a quintuple-mutant, multifluorescent, immunocompetent osteosarcoma model with postnatal p53 and rb1 inactivation. Osterix-expressing fluorescent tumor cells enter circulation upon tumor development and predominate in lung metastases, and the tumor immune landscape mimics human disease, enabling real-time analysis of progression, metastasis, and therapy testing.

papers.title: Gliadin-specific CD4(+) T cells exhibit functional diversity independent of TCR usage or epitope specificity.
papers.summary: Single-cell transcriptomic and TCR profiling of gliadin-specific CD4+ T cells from celiac patients after gluten challenge reveals TH1 effector, regulatory, and cytotoxic phenotypes across epitope specificities, with no epitope-driven specialization. Core TCR motifs governing gliadin epitope specificity and cross-reactivity were identified, enabling specificity prediction from unassigned TCRs.

papers.title: A TERRA-NONO axis drives fibroblast reprogramming in cancer.
papers.summary: The lncRNA TERRA is consistently elevated in cancer-associated fibroblasts from skin, lung, and breast tumors. Loss of androgen receptor repression permits TERRA-NONO complex formation, which reprograms gene expression to drive CAF activation; TERRA silencing or pharmacologic NONO inhibition reverses CAF activation and suppresses tumor-stroma interactions in vivo.

papers.title: Transposon end recognition and pairing by I-F3 CRISPR-associated transposase.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structure of the VchCAST transposase TnsB bound to transposon DNA ends and host factor IHF reveals how asymmetric left and right transposon ends are recognized and paired. End pairing creates a previously uncharacterized protein interface required for transposition, informing CAST engineering for genome-editing applications.

papers.title: Trans-Eurasian steppe herder and barley farmer migrations shaped paternal genomic dynamics in Northwest China and Hui evolution.
papers.summary: Using 1,053 newly sequenced Y chromosomes, researchers reconstructed Eurasian spatiotemporal paternal phylogeny, identifying 15,810 previously unknown variants. Bronze Age Xinjiang was dominated by Xiaohe-related and western steppe herder lineages, with later East Asian farmer and steppe pastoralist contributions; modern Altaic-speaking populations show strong Iron Age paternal continuity.

papers.title: Once yearly cell-based therapy for sustained and dose-tunable delivery of monoclonal antibodies.
papers.summary: An encapsulated, immunomodulatory alginate cell-based "biologics factory" enables continuous in vivo monoclonal antibody production from a single administration, sustaining anti-HIV 3BNC117 titers for one year in mice and ipilimumab for over six months in nonhuman primates, with a retrievable macrodevice allowing dose-proportional tuning and on-demand termination.

papers.title: S-Nitrosylation of glycogen phosphorylase regulates nuclear glycogenolysis and is impaired in metabolic liver disorders.
papers.summary: Nuclear glycogen storage marks livers in argininosuccinic aciduria and MASLD. Nitric oxide promotes S-nitrosylation of glycogen phosphorylase (PYGL) at cysteine-446, driving hnrnpf-mediated nuclear translocation and nuclear glycogenolysis that sustains histone acetylation; NO supplementation restored nuclear PYGL in vivo, defining a mechanism for metabolic liver disorders.

papers.title: Aging-associated SATB1 deficiency remodels 3D genome architecture and transcriptional programs in naive CD4(+) T cells.
papers.summary: Aging naive CD4+ T cells show proinflammatory, proactivation transcriptional reprogramming alongside weakened topologically associating domain boundaries and enhancer-promoter rewiring. Declining SATB1, which normally constrains CTCF-binding sites together with CTCF, partly explains these changes; conditional Satb1 deletion in naive T cells recapitulates the aged 3D genome and transcriptional state.

papers.title: Synapse-like specializations at dopamine release sites orchestrate efficient and precise neuromodulatory signaling.
papers.summary: Dopamine release is not broadcast stochastically: axonal varicosities form direct, synapse-like appositions with D1- or D2-receptor-expressing somata and dendrites, and ALFA-tagged receptor knock-in mice show receptor puncta preferentially positioned near release sites. This spatial coupling supports precise, efficient neuromodulatory signaling across striatum, amygdala, and prefrontal cortex.

papers.title: DeCoRE: A computational method to resolve RNA structural heterogeneity from RNA structure probing data by direct RNA sequencing.
papers.summary: DeCoRE resolves RNA structural heterogeneity at single-nucleotide resolution from direct RNA sequencing of structure-probing data. It recovers known riboswitch alternative conformations and reveals a previously uncharacterized cotranscriptional folding pathway of bacterial ribosomal RNA in which two conformations coexist during early elongation before converging on the mature fold.

papers.title: Reappraising the topology of cell-free fetal DNA in maternal blood toward improved prenatal genetic diagnostics.
papers.summary: This review appraises current knowledge of the origin, release into maternal circulation, and structural topology of cell-free fetal DNA. Clarifying cffDNA biology could address the bottlenecks limiting noninvasive prenatal testing-low fetal fraction, maternal-fetal discrimination, and genotype discordance-advancing NIPT from screening toward comprehensive prenatal genetic diagnostics.

papers.title: Tumor gasdermin E acts as a rheostat to limit apoptotic cell survival and mutagenesis in anticancer immune environments.
papers.summary: Gasdermin E caps caspase activity before membrane rupture during apoptosis. Its loss permits survival of cells sustaining caspase-activated DNase-mediated DNA damage, enabling propagation of mutated clones; TCGA tumors with low GSDME expression and high immune signatures show higher mutational burden, linking GSDME to immune-driven mutagenesis control.

papers.title: Toward transgenic multicellular parasites: CRISPR-Cas12a germline editing of Schistosoma mansoni eggs as key to success.
papers.summary: An optimized RNP-based editing platform for Schistosoma mansoni shows Cas12a outperforms Cas9 for homology-directed insertion at a genomic safe-harbor site. EGFP-marked transgenic parasites were carried through the full life cycle with stable chromosomal integration and germline transmission, establishing transgenesis for a parasite genus previously lacking genetic tools.

papers.title: Remodeling of mitochondrial dynamics by metabolic pathways couples to oncogenic growth in GNAS (Gα(s)) mutant pancreas cancer.
papers.summary: In pancreatic cancers with concurrent KRAS G12D and GNAS R201C/H mutations, hyperactive GNAS maintains mitochondria in a fused state necessary for tumor growth despite mutant KRAS. The branched-chain amino acid pathway, TCA cycle, and aspartate metabolism converge on NAD+/NADH availability to promote mitochondrial fusion.

papers.title: Functional diversification of CsCAD14 orchestrates synergistic phenylpropanoid biosynthesis to defend gray blight disease in tea plants.
papers.summary: Tea plant CsCAD14 exhibits dual enzymatic activity, producing both monolignols and hydroxycinnamic acids that synergistically inhibit Pestalotiopsis gray blight. A nonsynonymous mutation abolishing dual activity associates with pathogen susceptibility, and evolutionary analysis traces CAD functional diversification from single-activity in algae to dual-activity enzymes in land plants.

papers.title: Deep learning-enhanced single-shot triorganelle STED-FLIM imaging of lipid dynamics in living cells.
papers.summary: A single-shot STED-FLIM workflow combining Nile Red analogs with deep-learning demultiplexing maps lipid dynamics simultaneously across endoplasmic reticulum, lipid droplets, and mitochondria in living cells. A lightweight VGG16-UNet enables automated tri-compartment quantification, capturing ferroptosis- and apoptosis-associated lipid remodeling during stress at nanoscale, lifetime-encoded resolution.

papers.title: Speech clocks decode dementia phenotypes, social exposome, and biological aging.
papers.summary: A speech-based aging clock trained on 2,928 individuals across five Latin American countries derives speech age gaps that differentiate healthy controls, mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and frontotemporal dementia. Gaps correlate with phosphorylated tau, brain clocks, epigenetic age, and social exposome, offering a scalable, low-cost biomarker.

papers.title: Silver(I)-mediated amide-to-ester transformation on unprotected peptides for protein chemical synthesis and engineering.
papers.summary: A silver(I)-mediated amide-to-ester transformation using an easily introduced N,S-benzylidene thioacetal scaffold converts backbone amides of unprotected peptides to salicylaldehyde esters in aqueous acetic acid without detectable epimerization, enabling serine/threonine ligation and the total synthesis of mirror-image histones H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.

papers.title: Restoring brain functions in the Mo-blo mouse model of Menkes disease with copper nanoclusters.
papers.summary: In ATP7A-deficient Mo-blo mice, daily subcutaneous ultrasmall copper nanoclusters crossed the blood-brain barrier, normalized cuproenzyme activities, and restored cognitive and motor function while improving survival-unlike standard copper-histidine therapy-suggesting a first disease-modifying approach for the fatal neurodegeneration of Menkes disease.

papers.title: Predicting and finding geroprotective compounds through modulating conserved longevity-associated aging modules.
papers.summary: Deconstructing the aging transcriptome into coexpression modules modulated by lifespan-extending interventions in C. elegans, researchers built a model that predicted and validated 10 geroprotective compounds, seven previously unreported. Several longevity-associated modules are conserved in mice and correlate with frailty, providing a framework for geroprotector discovery.

papers.title: A noncanonical function of the tyrosine degradation enzyme FAH drives CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance in breast cancer.
papers.summary: Fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase (FAH) translocates to the nucleus upon CDK4/6 inhibition in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, interacting with CDK9 to drive resistance. Nuclear FAH is enriched in tumors from relapsed patients, and CDK9 inhibition reverses FAH-mediated resistance, establishing a resistance biomarker and therapeutic vulnerability.

papers.title: Multiobjective V(H)H discovery through integrated high-throughput screening and AlphaFold3-guided structural prioritization.
papers.summary: Combining high-throughput yeast display screening, deep sequencing, and AlphaFold3-guided structural triage, researchers discovered polyspecific VHH antibodies against long-chain alpha-neurotoxins that bind conserved epitopes across snake toxins and block acetylcholine receptor binding. The pipeline offers a structure-guided filter reducing experimental screening for broad-neutralization antibody discovery.

papers.title: A forward genetics platform for papillomavirus research.
papers.summary: A phenotypic selection platform for human papillomavirus links genotype to phenotype through "concordant" virus libraries in which each mutant particle encapsidates its encoding plasmid. It achieves roughly 2,500-fold enrichment of L1 mutants and enabled isolation of antibody escape mutants, unlocking HPV forward genetics for vaccine and antiviral work.

papers.title: The protein tyrosine phosphatase interactome: beyond catalytic activity.
papers.summary: This review frames protein tyrosine phosphatases as scaffolds organizing spatially constrained signaling complexes rather than mere kinase antagonists. Integrating interactome-mapping advances for SHP-2, PTPN23, PTPN13, PTPRM, and PTPRK across cancer, neurobiology, and immune signaling, it highlights scaffold-dependent disease mechanisms and therapeutic strategies targeting phosphatase protein-protein interactions.

papers.title: Blood cell composition reveals distinct biological interpretation of DNA methylation age and age acceleration.
papers.summary: Using a collinearity-robust principal component approach across 4,058 samples, blood cell composition-especially the naive-to-memory T cell balance-explains up to 53% of DNA methylation age variance, with weaker links to age acceleration. Cell composition only modestly attenuated associations with 176 incident health outcomes among 18,859 individuals.

papers.title: Distinct roles for TANGO1S domains in maintaining ER-Golgi architecture.
papers.summary: Expressing TANGO1S domain-deletion mutants in TANGO1L/S knockout cells maps domain roles in ER-Golgi maintenance: TANGO1 loss causes cis-Golgi vesiculation not rescued by TANGO1S re-expression, the TEER domain is essential for ER organization, and TEER, CC2, and PRD domains are required for a defined ERGIC.

papers.title: Tubulin polyglutamylation modulates Golgi morphodynamics and neurite branching during neuronal morphogenesis.
papers.summary: In human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, tubulin polyglutamylation depletion disrupts somatic Golgi morphology and associated organelle interactions, slows anterograde transport of Golgi-derived compartments in proximal neurites, and increases neurite branching and tortuosity-linking a microtubule post-translational modification to organelle organization and neuronal morphogenesis.
